page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, providing 4 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 959 GB SSD. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The virtualization layer is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.i2.xlarge exhibits lower-tier performance across multiple compute and memory metrics. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% of benchmarked instances. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 163.34 GB/sec, which drops to 19.71 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, placing it in the bottom 10%. Geekbench testing aligns with these findings, with a single-core score of 934.0 and a multi-core score of 2030.0, both placing in the bottom 10%. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show limitations, with single-threaded gzip compression registering at 18.97 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.3 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i2.xlarge offers a high ratio of local SSD storage and memory relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it a viable option for workloads that require local data caching or moderate memory capacity without demanding high CPU throughput. However, its weak processing performance and low memory bandwidth present clear tradeoffs for compute-intensive tasks. Passmark database operations scored 1083.99, and Redis SET operations achieved 2.95 million operations per second. This profile suggests the instance is best suited for lightweight database hosting, local file caching, basic web serving, or general-purpose workloads that can tolerate lower CPU and memory performance in exchange for local SSD capacity.
